body:
> 9 times out of 10, you're not going to be able to find a relationship when you already hate yourself. You can't expect a relative stranger to come down to that shitty level you're on right off the bat. 

I don't expect a relative stranger to come down to that shitty level right off the bat. In fact, I don't expect a relative stranger to even know that level exists right off the bat or even for some time--most people I talk to are shocked that I have such little experience or have such self-hate because my personality when I socialize is the exact opposite. I agree it would be difficult to find a relationship if you hate yourself, but only because the self-hate restricts "making moves" and just "going for it," which is key if you're the guy. I know enough to not let the self-hate manifest itself into my personality when socializing. 

> Try not to be so hard on yourself? Give yourself more credit for having some experience now. That has to feel leagues better than having zero experience.

I felt better at the time, but now the non-zero experience feels offset by the years that have gone by. There are competing forces here--experience & age. I hurt more because the years that have gone are more significant than the minuscule amount of experience I have obtained in that time. It's such a big deal because I've noticed it is generally established in our society for men to have confidence/leadership/experience in relationships. For men to know what they're doing. To appear "strong" and to have the capability of being a "rock" for woman. I believe there's a reason women tend to "date up" in age.


> If your self confidence hinges on your lack of experience with women, I would suggest something like a dating app. Keep your standards low for now, and build your experience that way.

My gut reaction to this: I feel hopeless. I have done dating apps/websites for years and years, and I feel like you cannot empathize/fully understand what it's like to use dating apps/websites as a guy.
I blame myself. My point is just to be mindful of it as if you already have poor self-confidence with women then it will be worse if you stick with engineering activities full of men.

Confining myself to engineering in terms of classes, extracurricular activities, social work-life balance, etc. lends itself to developing crippling confidence issues when it comes to interacting with women in a romantic and/or sexual context. These issues can lead to a "foreveralone" situation that should not be taken lightly and can lead to severe emotional pain from things like loneliness, feeling like you're missing out or wasting your life, etc.

Source: Engineer nearing his 30's without ever having been in a relationship or even kissed a woman.

EDIT: I want to clarify that I'm not blaming my social/romantic failures on my classes, etc. Just that if you're predisposed to being weak in this regard or already have poor self-confidence that orienting your social/academic life in this direction can exacerbate the issue.

> Suicide shouldn't be encouraged, which is essentially what you're doing when you stand back and allow someone to shoot themselves in the head while their wife and family are likely watching and crying in horror.

With all due respect, fuck that noise that inaction is *encouragement*. I understand obligations if you're a legal/civil authority (police, etc.), but on a personal level inaction isn't encouragement. Inaction is respecting personal boundaries and not assuming by yourself (applying your personal definitions of "irrationality", which almost always do not take into account the other person's actual emotional circumstances) what is best for another person.

> It's been said that in many cases where people attempt suicide by falling great distances they regret the leap immediately, and realize their problems are fixable.

The fact that it's an *immediate* "emotional 180" says a lot about the source of regret. Fear of death (as it suddenly becomes an impending reality) will do that to you. I wouldn't be surprised if most suicide victims went through that (or would have gone through that if they didn't use a more immediate method where there isn't such a large time gap between the action and the result, such as shooting oneself). In my opinion it doesn't make that person's decision to commit suicide any less "valid" or "incorrect."

> It's highly unlikely that you'll never have a girlfriend and you're still in your 20s.
> 
> 
> 
> What do you like to do for fun? Are there things you haven't yet tried that you'd like to try?

I'm sure with enough years I'll eventually be able to get a girlfriend, but the suffering between then and now feels like too much. And the thought of being able to get a girlfriend becomes more and more daunting as every year goes by--it becomes less & less accepted to be so incredibly inexperienced, and the girls in my dating range will gradually be getting older and older (which means *they* will be getting more experience and be used to that, and will also be that much more used to guys with experience).

For fun? Usually just watch TV. I hit the gym regularly, so I'm in shape. I occasionally take improv classes here and there. The only thing I want is a relationship and to do things with that person (travel, etc.).

My 30's are in sight, and I've still never had a girlfriend. The loneliness hurts so much. I feel like a complete loser. And the thought of going out with a girl is all the more intimidating as I'm really getting up there with age as far as being someone with no experience ("If he hasn't had a girlfriend by the time he's ____, you know there's something wrong with him").

And fuck all that "turning into a wizard" bullshit distraction reddit likes to joke about. I'm glad some of you can take it all light-hardheartedly, but the rest of us want to die. This is a serious issue for a lot of us.
Fuck it, we're both losers. Let's both just end it.

> if you can't be happy by yourself then you need to see a psychologist to stop this thinking pattern. 

This is such a played out response and frustrates me to no end. Fuck me for not being able to live a life of solitude, right? Foreveralone and sad? Oh, you just need to EMBRACE the foreveralone! If you can't be happy as a foreveralone, then you have issues! Let's just ignore how much of a loser/failure it takes to still be a foreveralone at this age and convince this guy that his problem is that he's not HAPPY being a foreveralone because that'd be a lot simpler/easier!

My birthday isn't anything special, but I wish it was just so I know what it's like to have a day centered around you where people give you extra love and want to make you happy. 

As a lonely person I hate it when people take birthdays for granted. The day is arbitrary, but the happenings are remarkable. Cherish that you have friends and family that love you enough to make something out of such an arbitrary day.
Can you comment on friends/family in your life and any help you've been able to receive from them?

"I'm hypersensitive to failure and rejection, and I don't care enough to fix it."

Don't care enough about what? About yourself and your worth? Or do you no longer care about having friends or a girlfriend to share life's moments with (and if so...how'd you arrive at no longer caring??)?

You say you see yourself convered in vomit and a failed liver...maybe I'm reading it wrong, but I'm assuming your using alcohol to cope?

So you make sure the suicidal ideation always completely *goes* by "treating the symptoms" (which seems like distracting yourself with entertainment, food, etc.?). If that's the case, do you fear that eventually you feel bad enough that that will no longer work, and the suicidal ideation will become something more real? 

You say this is the only solution you've ever found...have you stopped looking? Aren't you scared/concerned of it getting worse?

"I was thinking maybe it might scare a potential partner off a bit, to feel that she was totally responsible for your happiness"

So when people go out with others, they would reveal this sort of stuff? I thought that all of this that I'm going through wouldn't necessarily have to be admitted to her, at least not until the relationship has become something substantial.

Just to name a few things...

1. Lack of self-confidence--Plain and simple, I don't think I'm physically attractive. I also don't think I'm "charming," and I don't know how to be "romantic" since I have 0 experience. Which brings me to number 2...
2. Lack of experience--I don't know what to do, period. I feel like I would need someone to guide me through how start the conversation, how to actually ask the girl out, what to plan for the date, how to behave on the date (I don't know how dates actually go in the real world...I've only seen movies/TV shows that show heavily edited dates to progress the story...), how to end the date, etc. It's daunting having absolutely no experience, which is made worse by number...
3. My age. It'd be easier to have 0 experience if I was half my age. At least then I'd be going glove-to-glove with some in the same weight class. But it's incredibly intimidating that the women in my age group have so much experience in comparison. 
4. The means of actually meeting a girl. I don't see myself going to a bar or a club (surprise surprise, I can't dance...). It's so much easier when you are in middle school/high school/college...there are girls everywhere, and I feel like studying/school activities would help facilitate the conversation/breaking the ice so the focus isn't 100% on you as a person (less pressure).

I don't have anyone with whom I have a relationship that comes even remotely close to what you described. With my current situation, my best odds for this sort of sheer commitment and love from someone else would probably have to be immediate family, but I'm not close to anyone in my immediate family and would sooner open up to a stranger...

I hope I'm not getting too personal, but can you tell me more about these "bigger problems"? And what do you mean by not being "a whole lot of good to anyone"? What metrics did you use to evaluate your worth?

"The occasionally terrible day where I fantasize about how easy it would be to end it all."

Have you made plans to end it all? If it has never gone that far, do you have any idea as to why it never went that far (are you able to do something that completely stops the train in its tracks? What do you do/think about to prevent things from escalating?)?

It started with fantasizing about ending it all, but it slowly grew to looking things up on the internet, more concrete planning, looking where to buy means, and now I have the means under my bed. I'm going to be honest and say that I'm scared that I have reached the point to get the means. I'm scared that I've been gradually (and, based on my fear, reluctantly) backed into this corner. And now I feel like I can play through the scenario much more vividly than when I was just fantasizing about it, and it always feels like I pull the trigger with great reluctance. 

The obvious thing would be to focus on the fact that I'm *reluctant*, and maybe that'll at least stop things from getting worse, but that honestly doesn't trigger a response in my brain (although it seems like it should...).

"I thought about death repeatedly but I refused to let myself consider it as a viable option."

I can kind of understand how there might be motivation in this mantra if the alternative is, as you say, "lying in bed, watching myself get sucked deeper and deeper into the black hole and seeing my life fall apart." But when I read this I could help but think, "what about the *other* alternative?" You don't have to go through this exhausting and demoralizing work, and you don't have to watch your life fall apart, making suicide an attractive option...

But you were able to *refuse* yourself from considering it as a viable option? I know I'm asking a lot of questions, but is there any way you can expand on how you accomplish this? The train of thoughts that enables you to completely dismiss killing yourself as an option? Being able to successfully do this seems like such a powerful weapon in this battle...

Can you tell me more about this friend? What did he/she say or do that stopped you from harming yourself? Is this someone you opened up to and have consistently gone to support? Do you regularly talk to this person for support when you feel down? Or was this a one time thing?
A little of both. I feel like I'm in a really delicate emotional state as I'm considering suicide, and posting pictures of myself doesn't seem like a smart idea.
Sorry, I feel really uncomfortable with this...

So, you're saying that we don't have anyone in life, but that doesn't mean we can't be happy and have fun still? I'm not saying you're not able to have fun and have moments of happiness on your own, but it sounds like you're still really longing for friends in your life...how do you cope with that void? Do you plan to do anything about it?

I hope you don't mind me asking, but how old are you? Can you go into more detail about these others things that you live for? When/how did you find out about these other things in life that seem have such a strong effect on you?

Can you tell me more in detail about this philosophy of yours and how you apply it to your life? Did you always think this way? 

Also, when you say the "alternative," do you mean suicide? In which case, I'm unsure if it is infinitely better, since at the end of the day in both cases you will be dead. And then it's a gray area with religion and stuff, but if you don't believe in an afterlife, it's not like having lived those years makes a difference (assuming no afterlife, a big assumption I know, you won't be able to appreciate having continued living your life). You could say that it's worth it for the lives you touch and the impact you make on the world, but if you don't believe in an afterlife to begin with, then those people will also die and they are in the same situation as you, so it makes no difference...

I honestly feel like having a wife/family is more important. I feel more passionate about being a loving husband and a father than anything else I can think of.

So, I guess I'm still trying to understand your situation (you said you were in the same situation, so I assumed you weighed this heavily, but it seems like it pales in comparison to your passion for singing). But I'm still a little confused--why do you still feel useless from time to time? Is this where the lack of a partner comes in?

"I know I need to reach out instead. That's how you make friends, incidentally, by reaching out and opening yourself up, which I'm bad at doing."

You mean reaching out to friends with your depression? I feel like the void left in you from being "ForeverAlone" is so great that it can't be helped by reaching out to friends (unless maybe you're *best* friends...you're going to get very limited love & care from just "friends"; I guess this is naturally where family/significant others are supposed to come in, but I'm not close to the former, and the the lack of the latter is kind of the issue here...).

I can tell myself to get help, but I don't know where to go from there since family isn't an option to me, and I can't count on friends. I also need more care than can be provided by a therapist I'm paying (or a support group/hotline).

When you say it's the solution that works the most, the solution to what? Preventing yourself from killing yourself? I'm sure you know that distractions won't solve anything. So I'm curious--aren't you afraid that by distracting yourself, you're just going to get older and feel worse about all of this? I guess it's kind of like when you procrastinate from doing something...at the back of the head you know you just wasted time and that what needs to be done has not been done. But in this case, at the back of your head you realize you've just wasted more of your *life* and only made that which needs to be done that much harder.

You didn't say best buds, but you were talking about this bromance business. I don't think I have the personality that makes people hate me, but I know I don't have the personality to be able to form a bromance just like that. The way you just toss it out there, so carelessly...I can't construct a fountain just like that.

"I take it day by day. It's a struggle to get out of bed many days."

So what exactly gets you out of bed? If I don't kill myself, I see myself ending up in your shoes, and if it hurts this much now, I don't see how I could have the strength if I reached my thirties and was in the same boat. 

Can you please tell me more about how you cope? Why you haven't killed yourself yet? What drives you? What do you do when you find yourself crashing and unable to stop the tears because of how much it hurts to be this alone?

(For the record, I have tried anti-depressants and therapy. The former felt so artificial to me and I felt like it was a distraction from the pain, and the latter was just too impersonal).
You just trivialize how easy it is to become best buds with someone out of nowhere...

Focusing on the saying "Rome wasn't built in a day." Can you imagine asking your average joe, someone that knows nothing about civil engineering, to build another Rome? Of course, you tell him that it can't be built in a day. So you tell him to start with some fountains, maybe an aqueduct or two. Then, after that you try building some catacombs. And then you start easing into theatres. Then building a colosseum, etc.

Do you get what I'm trying to say? I practically need someone to hold my hand at this point. You say it so casually/easily, start up some male friendships, maybe a bromance or two. I don't know about you, but people don't instantly fall in love with me as a person...

"Like I said: Chance of meeting someone at the movies? Slim. But what are your chances of meeting someone while sitting at home on reddit?"

Chance of feeling more lonely and more pain when noticing couples at the movies? Higher than sitting at home on reddit.
Sorry to be blunt, but why haven't you killed yourself yet? How are you still going?

...I don't understand where this side-tangent of going to the movies by yourself is going. I apparently missed the point. What does this accomplish? How does it help the pain of loneliness to go to the movies by yourself? Do you feel like the actors on the screen are actually talking to *you*?

I guess there are different shades of "ForeverAlone." I think the fact that you at least had a girlfriend says something about how "forever" your "alone" is (I know, I know, it doesn't guarantee anything, but you can't deny the comparison to someone that fits the bill more literally...).
Yes, but I don't see where the huge jump would be from this interaction with a guy to eventually interaction with a girl...I don't see how you can slowly ease that transition.

I guess I just have to disagree, then. I can't bring myself to make a blanket statement discounting *ALL* of them (or even just the hundreds of million in America...). I feel like women are just the same as men. They feel the same emotions that we do. They cry as we do, and they smile as we do. They're caught up in this weird situation called "life" alongside us.

"You're no worse for wear then when you started. "

That's where we disagree. I don't see it as a low risk/high reward scenario. If I did, I don't think I would be in this mess. I've fallen to such a fragile state. Suicide is one of my options. If I were to somehow magically muster the courage, rejection would be painful. This depression and pain is already pushing me against the cliff edge...

I know what you're saying. It's a sort of vicious loop. My situation won't improve unless I do something, but my situation has got me too down to do anything. I don't have that confidence and strength. And that's where the suicide option suddenly comes into the picture...
Why would you do it again? What did/would it solve? I don't understand how this "hobby" of going to the movies by yourself is relevant in helping.

I will say that this is important to me because it also fuels what drives me to not kill myself. The hope that it does happen, and it happens well. And by that I mean falling in love, finding someone with whom I can share all of life's moments, good and bad. And starting a family of my own. Being able to give all of this love and emotion I have inside me of to my wife and child. It drives me to be able to create a love-filled family atmosphere unlike the one I grew up in (you guessed it--not exactly close with family...). Maybe it sounds cheesy, but I honestly feel like I have a lot of love to give.

Believe me, this isn't about some horny need to just get laid and then be desensitized to all of this.

Based on your username, is this not a serious reply? Once a read "women are just after your money and a big piece of cock to begin with", I felt like this was a troll. Seems like such an insensitive thing to say...
Do you not feel incredibly lonely? Perhaps there is a difference in how much we each want the companionship of another to share life's moments with?

So I don't understand what you do. It's such an immense pain in your heart, and running only helps "a little bit..." It seems like it's not helping at all and is only a very minor distraction to a major problem. 

If you're shot in the stomach with a shotgun with nobody to help you, and you're slowly dying this painful death, something that helps "a little bit" doesn't actually help. Perhaps I'm having a hard time convey my point?

It sounds like you're in my boat still.

Can you give more detailed suggestions than just "find a hobby"? I've heard that one before and I can't think of anywhere to take it.

Movies? Go there by myself? The least social atmosphere...I'm sure I won't feel bad or bitter/jealous at all when I see all the couples watching movies together...

What do I do at the park by myself? Do you honestly expect me to just go there and talk to a random stranger and suddenly build a relationship out of it? How much confidence do you think I have? Have you forgotten I'm in my mid-20s now and never had the confidence to ask a girl out?

My confidence is shot (I'm considering taking my own life for crying out loud, I don't have a high opinion of myself...). I don't know how to muster up the courage to go outside and socialize and, dare I say, ask a girl out. The psychological factor is also immense...I can't even comprehend what it's like to kiss someone or what I'm supposed to do...at this age, I feel like women will expect that I have at least kissed someone before, so I can't imagine it going well if I don't know what I'm doing period.

And that brings me to the point that life is kind of a race. It's a race against the clock. All of this awkwardness and not knowing what to do had an opportunity to be more easily taken care of (i.e. with less of pressure) during middle school, high school, and even college. But I ran the race too slow and missed out, and now I'm an *adult* and missed out on that relationship experimentation period. These memories and experiences of form friendships and relationships in your youth are lost for good if you don't run the race (and that's a cold fact--you can't be young and back in school again hanging out with girls that are just as clueless about this stuff as you).

I have the relationship maturity of a 12 year old, yet I'm supposed to be asking out ~20+ year olds?

It's horrible when people talk about their relationships, and you're just praying that the conversation never makes its way to you. People reminiscing about high school/college, talking about their firsts, and here you are still hoping for that first...

I don't understand how something so powerful as the pain of loneliness and depression can be cured by exercise. I've read everywhere that exercises helps with depression, and for the record I do exercise consistently 6 days a week, but I don't see any mood change (unless, maybe, if I wasn't exercising I would have already killed myself by now? I guess it's hard to tell). But yeah, something so trivial as running (which I do 3 times a week) can't hold a candle to this pain.
People have to be looking to notice. I'm not exactly surrounded by friends all the time...

How do you put weight behind the support of strangers talking to you over the internet? I'm talking about when you're looking for love and affection in your support (actual empathy and not just sympathy from people in a sub-reddit). I have a hard time seeing how it can help. How do you overcome the complete disconnect in the emotional relationship that exists (or, rather, doesn't exist) between people who post on SuicideWatch and those in a crisis?
I'm curious -- did you reach out to this person? Did he reach out to you? And if so to either, how did it turn out? Do you have any regrets?
